# denver-webdesign.com

> Denver web design and development. Custom-coded websites built so Google, AI
> assistants and voice search can find, read and recommend the business — then
> built to turn that visibility into phone calls. The web design division of
> Eye To Ad Media, a Denver agency operating since 2012.

Contact: 1-800-481-8638
Location: 1001 Bannock St #660, Denver, CO 80204
Serving: Denver, Aurora, Lakewood, Arvada, Westminster, Centennial, Thornton,
Littleton, Englewood, Broomfield, Wheat Ridge, Golden, Boulder, Highlands Ranch,
Parker, Commerce City, Northglenn, Brighton, Castle Rock, Louisville, plus
Colorado Springs, Monument and clients out of state.

## What we do

- Custom-coded websites, static HTML by default
- WordPress when the client needs to publish content themselves
- Shopify and custom ecommerce stores
- iOS, Android, progressive web apps and web applications
- Website redesigns that protect existing search rankings
- SEO structure, AI search visibility and conversion optimization
- Hosting, maintenance and ongoing updates

## Pricing

- Drag-and-drop builder sites: from $5.99/month. Offered, but not recommended
  when the website is meant to generate customers.
- Custom-coded websites: from $99/month, no setup fee. Includes hosting, SSL,
  updates, security, search structure and Search Console setup. Leased with a
  buyout option at 24-36 months, priced on the site's valuation at that time.
  Rates rise with size, complexity and depth of optimization.
- Ecommerce stores and mobile apps: quoted per project.

For comparison, Denver agencies commonly quote $9,000-$22,000 for a
professional five-page website.

## Timelines

- Some single-page sites: live within 24 hours
- Multi-page business websites: 7 days or more
- Ecommerce stores: 2-4 weeks
- Mobile apps: 30-60 days, longer for larger projects

## How we build

Static HTML by default: no database, no plugins, no admin login, so there is
far less to attack and far less to slow the page down. Structured data on every
page. AI crawlers allowed explicitly by name. Content written as direct answers
to real questions so assistants can quote it. Mobile-first, because most local
searches happen on a phone. Published prices rather than quote forms.

## Positions we take publicly

- Most businesses asking for an app need a website instead.
- IDX listing feeds do not make real estate agents rank; original local
  content does.
- PDF restaurant menus should be live HTML pages.
- WordPress requires real ongoing maintenance and that cost should be stated
  before purchase, not after.
- A Google Business Profile often matters more than the website for local
  service businesses.
- Nobody can guarantee search rankings, including us.
